chunks: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'May Allah make me your ransom, a tradition has reached us from you.' He asked: 'What is it?' I said: 'Your saying: The possessor of this affair will only be delighted when it reaches here,' and he pointed with his hand to his throat. He said: 'Yes, indeed the people of this affair will be delighted when it reaches here,' and he gestured with his hand to his throat. 'As for that which he feared from the world, it will have passed away from him, and his Imam will be the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), and Al-Hasan and Al-Husayn (peace be upon them).'

key_terms.حَلْقُهُ: his throat (symbolizing the approach of death)
key_terms.صَاحِبُ الْأَمْرِ: the possessor of the affair (referring to the Imam/Mahdi)

ai.seo_question: What happens to the Imam's fears and companions at the moment of death according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) identifies the 'throat' (al-halq) as the point of death, confirming that the leader of the true believers experiences delight at this moment as worldly anxieties depart. This transition is spiritually supported by the presence of the Prophet Muhammad, Ali, Hasan, and Husayn (peace be upon them), reflecting the Shia belief in the continuity of divine guidance and intercession through the Ahl al-Bayt.
